text:
Local News
Marshall Co. teacher, husband killed at home; suspect killed in officer-involved shooting
Trending
MOUNDSVILLE -- A 25-year-old Moundsville man shot and killed a John Marshall High School teacher and her husband early Thursday morning because of past grievances and his interest in their juvenile daughter, said Marshall County Sheriff Mike Dougherty.
Cyle Fabrizio shot to death JMHS teacher Monica Will and her husband David with the Wills’ two children in the home, Dougherty said. Deputies responded to the residence after Marshall County 911 received a call at 1:40 a.m.; no one spoke on the line.
As deputies approached the Wills’ home, Dougherty said Fabrizio fired at them with a pistol. The deputies took cover and tried to determine where the gunfire was coming from. Fabrizio then appeared at the doorway holding a juvenile girl hostage with a pistol to her head.
“Faced with an immediate threat to the juvenile's life, a deputy armed with a rifle fired one shot, striking Fabrizio and stopping the threat,” Dougherty said. “Fabrizio died as a result of the shooting.”
When the deputies entered the house, Dougherty said they found the bodies of both David Will, 44, and Monica Will, 46. Both victims had sustained gunshot wounds. Dougherty said evidence indicates Fabrizio shot Monica Will through the home’s window while standing on the porch. Then he kicked down the door, entered the home and shot David Will.
Investigators have determined that Fabrizio had grievances with David and Monica Will stemming from a past incident and had an interest in their juvenile daughter, Dougherty said. Those circumstances remain part of the ongoing investigation. Neither the juvenile girl or boy were physically harmed, Dougherty added, and they are staying with family members.
"This was a tragic act of violence that has devastated a family and shocked our community," Dougherty said. "Our hearts are with the victims' children, their family members, and everyone affected by this senseless loss. My Deputy encountered an immediate, life-threatening situation and acted to save the life of a child."
The sheriff’s department is handling the homicide investigation, while the West Virginia State Police is handling the officer-involved shooting.
A joint message of condolence and support John Marshall High School Principal Jason Marling and Marshall County Schools Superintendent Shelby Haines has been released:
“John Marshall High School and Marshall County Schools are deeply saddened by the tragic loss of one of our teachers. Our thoughts are with her children, family, friends, and all of those who loved and cared for her.”
Because of the shooting, John Marshall High School closed Thursday morning just prior to the start of classes, with a parent noting children already had boarded buses.
Classes will resume Friday, but the planned homecoming parade scheduled for early Friday evening has been canceled.
“After much consideration and consultation, it has been decided that the homecoming parade will be canceled. All other homecoming and school-sponsored events will proceed beginning tomorrow.
“During this incredibly difficult time, we will continue to care for one another and support our students, staff, and families as we navigate this loss together. Supportive counseling is available at the school for students and staff.”
Most of the morning, sheriff’s deputies had the road closed near the house, only allowing local traffic to pass through. Yellow caution tape is around the perimeter of the two-story home located at the corner of Baywood Avenue and Fourth Street, which is about 50 yards from the Marshall County Schools Board of Education Office.
One man walking toward the scene said he wanted to check on his rental properties he owned nearby. He said he knew the family and was saddened by news of the homicide. He declined to give his name.
Another man who lives a few doors down from the crime scene said he did not know the couple, but he frequently takes walks in the neighborhood and was familiar with the house. He also declined to give his name.
The road block would be removed after deputies were finished processing the crime scene. Some traffic was being detoured off Fourth Street onto a side street so motorists could still get through.

Supportive counseling is available at the school for students and staff.” Most of the morning, sheriff’s deputies had the road closed near the house, only allowing local traffic to pass through.
